title: Little Office of the Most Sacred Five Wounds of Our Saviour Jesus Christ

introductoryNotes.text: From a book of the same name published in 1688.

translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine labia mea aperies.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance, etc.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, to help, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: ℟. Sicut erat, etc. Alleluja.
blocks.english: ℟. As it was, etc. Alleluia.

blocks.source: A Septuagesima usque ad Pascha loco Alleluja dicitur: Laus tibi Domine Rex aeternae Gloriae.
blocks.english: From Septuagesima until Easter, in place of Alleluia is said: Praise be to Thee, O Lord, King of everlasting glory.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Avete sacra Vulnera, In carne Christi fulgida, Nostrae salutis inclita Jam restitutae pignora.
blocks.english:
Hail, sacred Wounds,
Shining in the flesh of Christ,
Glorious pledges
Of our salvation now restored.

blocks.source: Manus ave te sauciae, Pedesque tincti sanguine, Diro pendentes stipite, Transfixi clavi cuspide.
blocks.english:
Hail, wounded hands,
And feet stained with blood,
Hanging upon the dreadful wood,
Pierced by the point of the nail.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints the split “ave te”; the greeting is rendered provisionally as hail, without changing the Latin.

blocks.source: Aveto Latus roseum, Tam late patens ostium Amanti Domicilium, Erranti Diversorium.
blocks.english:
Hail, rose-red Side,
A door opened so wide,
A home for the lover,
A lodging for the wanderer.

blocks.source: Laus tibi sit, et Gloria, Rex Christe pro victoria, Per sacra parta Vulnera, Magnae salutis Pretia.
blocks.english:
Praise and glory be to Thee,
Christ the King, for the victory
Won through Thy sacred Wounds,
The price of great salvation.

blocks.source: Antiphona Quid sunt plagae istae, in medio manuum tuarum? His plagatus sum in Domo eorum, qui me diligebant.
blocks.english: Antiphon. What are these wounds in the midst of Thy hands? With these I was wounded in the house of those who loved Me.

blocks.source: ℣. Foderunt manus meas et pedes meos:
blocks.english: ℣. They pierced My hands and My feet,

blocks.source: ℟. Et unus militum lancea Latus meum aperuit.
blocks.english: ℟. And one of the soldiers opened My Side with a spear.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe, Fili Dei vivi, qui ad aeterna redemptionis nostrae, et charitatis tuae monumenta, quinque Vulnerum Cicatrices in glorioso tuo Corpore retinere, easque post resurrectionem tuam discipulis tuis videndas et palpandas offerre voluisti: Concede, quaesumus, ut his fidei luminibus cum Thoma Apostolo illustrati, in divinae Benignitatis tuae oceano penitus absorbeamur, usque dum Majestatis tuae, et sacratissimorum Vulnerum tuorum Gloriam in coelo perenniter contemplaturi assumamur. Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitate Spiritus sancti Deus, per,
blocks.english: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who didst will to retain in Thy glorious Body the scars of five Wounds as everlasting memorials of our redemption and Thy charity, and after Thy resurrection to offer them to Thy disciples to see and touch, grant, we beseech Thee, that, enlightened with the Apostle Thomas by these lights of faith, we may be wholly immersed in the ocean of Thy divine loving kindness, until we are taken up to contemplate for ever in heaven the glory of Thy Majesty and Thy most sacred Wounds. Who livest and reignest with God the Father, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, through

blocks.source: etc.
blocks.english: etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Fidelium animae per misericordiam Dei requiescant in pace.
blocks.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

blocks.source: ℟. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. Amen.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance, etc.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Hic scatet fons viventibus, Exuberans liquoribus, Quinque decurrens amnibus De totidem canalibus.
blocks.english:
Here gushes a fount,
Abounding with living waters,
Flowing in five rivers
From as many channels.

blocks.source: Huc sine nummis pauperes, Huc properate divites, Huc sitientes animae, Quas urit amor, bibite.
Laus tibi sit, et Gloria, Rex Christe pro victoria, Per sacra parta vulnera, Magnae salutis Pretia.
blocks.english:
Praise and glory be to Thee,
Christ the King, for the victory
Won through Thy sacred Wounds,
The price of great salvation.

blocks.source: Antiphona Flumina coelestis Paradisi in Vulneribus Domini nostri Jesu Christi reserantur: quoniam apud eum est Fons vitae, et in ejus lumine videbimus lumen.
blocks.english: Antiphon. The rivers of heavenly Paradise are opened in the Wounds of our Lord Jesus Christ; for with Him is the fountain of life, and in His light we shall see light.

blocks.source: ℣. Haurietis aquas in gaudio de fontibus Salvatoris.
blocks.english: ℣. You shall draw waters with joy from the fountains of the Saviour,

blocks.source: ℟. Qui factus est vobis in salutem.
blocks.english: ℟. Who has become salvation for you.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe Fili Dei vivi, qui in cruce aperuisti nobis quinque fontes gratiarum, sicut aquarum viventium, quae fluunt impetu de Libano: Concede, ut extincta siti carnalis concupiscentiae, aestuque mundanae delictionis, in te solo sitiat anima nostra, et desideret ad has nobilissimas misericordiae tuae Venas, sicut cervus ad fontes aquarum: ut hauriamus vitam et salutem a te Jesu Salvatore nostro. Qui vivis et regnas, etc.
blocks.english: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who upon the Cross didst open for us five fountains of graces, like living waters flowing swiftly from Lebanon, grant that, the thirst of fleshly concupiscence and the heat of worldly delight being quenched, our soul may thirst for Thee alone, and long for these most noble veins of Thy mercy as the hart for the fountains of water, that we may draw life and salvation from Thee, Jesus our Saviour. Who livest and reignest, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “delictionis” is irregular; worldly delight is a provisional reading.

blocks.source: ℣. Fidelium animae, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful departed, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance, etc.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Hic Botrus, haec orantia Terrae promissae munera, Sub prelo crucis placida Desudat vini flumina.
blocks.english:
Here the cluster of grapes,
These [the printed “orantia” is uncertain] gifts of the promised land,
Beneath the gentle press of the Cross
Pour forth rivers of wine.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “orantia”; its intended adjective is uncertain and left marked rather than replaced by fragrant.

blocks.source: Sapore quae dulcedinis, Laetificant cor hominis. Cor levant ex angustiis, Mirisque mulcent gaudiis.
blocks.english:
Which with a savour of sweetness
Gladden the heart of man,
Lift the heart out of distress,
And soothe it with wondrous joys.

blocks.source: Laus tibi sit, et Gloria, Rex Christe pro victoria, Per sacra parta Vulnera, Magnae salutis Pretia.
blocks.english:
Praise and glory be to Thee,
Christ the King, for the victory
Won through Thy sacred Wounds,
The price of great salvation.

blocks.source: Antiphona Visitavit Dominus terram, et sanguine suo inebriavit eam, multiplicavit locupletavit eam.
blocks.english: Antiphon. The Lord visited the earth and watered it abundantly with His blood; He multiplied and enriched it.

blocks.source: ℣. Leo de tribu Juda lavit in vino Stolam suam.
blocks.english: ℣. The Lion of the tribe of Juda washed His robe in wine,

blocks.source: ℟. Et in sanguine uvae pallium suum.
blocks.english: ℟. And His mantle in the blood of the grape.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe Fili Dei vivi, qui de corpore tuo quinque pretiosissimi sanguinis flumina in remissionem peccatorum effudisti, quando in cruce torcular solus calcasti: Te humiliter deprecamur, reconcilia nos Deo in sanguine tuo quos tam copiose redemisti, et pota nos torrente hujus dulcedinis, ut ardentissima tui charitate inebriati portemus semper in corde nostro tua sacratissima amoris stigmata, unde pietate, gratia et justitia repleamur. Qui vivis et regnas, etc.
blocks.english: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who didst pour forth from Thy Body five rivers of most precious blood for the remission of sins, when upon the Cross Thou didst tread the winepress alone, we humbly beseech Thee: reconcile to God in Thy blood us whom Thou hast so abundantly redeemed, and give us to drink of the torrent of this sweetness, that, inebriated with most ardent charity for Thee, we may ever bear in our hearts Thy most sacred marks of love, whereby we may be filled with piety, grace and justice. Who livest and reignest, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Fidelium animae, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful departed, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance, etc.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Hic castrum non vincibile, Davidis Turri simile, Ac hostibus terribile, Huc fugiens te recipe.
blocks.english:
Here is an unconquerable fortress,
Like the tower of David,
And terrible to enemies;
Flee hither and take refuge.

blocks.source: Sunt quinque propugnacula, Fidelium refugia, Secura diversoria, Tutissima Praesidia.
blocks.english:
There are five bulwarks,
Refuges of the faithful,
Secure lodgings,
Most safe defences.

blocks.source: Laus tibi sit et Gloria, Rex Christe pro victoria, Per sacra parta Vulnera, Magnae salutis Pretia.
blocks.english:
Praise and glory be to Thee,
Christ the King, for the victory
Won through Thy sacred Wounds,
The price of great salvation.

blocks.source: Antiphona Ecce columba in foraminibus petrae, vulneribus Christi, crucis clypeo tecta, et armata clavis et lancea, omnis armatura fortium.
blocks.english: Antiphon. Behold the dove in the clefts of the rock, the Wounds of Christ, sheltered by the shield of the Cross and armed with nails and spear, all the armour of the mighty.

blocks.source: ℣. Videte manus meas, et pedes meos,
blocks.english: ℣. See My hands and My feet,

blocks.source: ℟. Ego sum, nolite timere.
blocks.english: ℟. It is I; fear not.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe Fili Dei vivi, qui nobis in sacratissimis tuis Vulneribus, in omni tribulatione et angustia tutum asylum, et singulare praesidium benignissime praeparasti: Libera nos, quaesumus, a vinculis iniquitatum, propter quas vulneratus es: et in omnibus mentis, corporis quae periculis abscondé nos intra tua Vulnera, ut non timeat cor nostrum, quoniam facta sunt illa nobis Turris fortitudinis a facie inimici. Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, etc.
blocks.english: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who hast most graciously prepared for us in Thy most sacred Wounds a safe refuge and singular defence in every tribulation and distress, deliver us, we beseech Thee, from the bonds of the iniquities for which Thou wast wounded; and in every peril of mind and body hide us within Thy Wounds, that our heart may not fear, for they have become for us a tower of strength before the enemy. Who livest and reignest with God the Father, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “corporis quae” and “abscondé”; the body-peril phrase is provisional.

blocks.source: ℣. Fidelium animae, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful departed, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance, etc.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Hic arbor vitae tenera Distendit quinque folia, Et umbrae suae suavia Largitur refrigeria.
blocks.english:
Here the tender tree of life
Spreads forth five leaves,
And grants the sweet refreshment
Of its shade.

blocks.source: Non urit hic sol radiis, Aut serpens mortis spiculis, Tot tutus es umbraculis, Quot arbor haec stat foliis.
blocks.english:
Here neither the sun with its rays
Nor the serpent with the darts of death burns;
Thou art safe beneath as many shelters
As this tree stands with leaves.

blocks.source: Laus tibi sit, et Gloria, Rex Christe pro victoria, Per sacra parta Vulnera, Magnae salutis Praetia.
blocks.english:
Praise and glory be to Thee,
Christ the King, for the victory
Won through Thy sacred Wounds,
The price of great salvation.

blocks.source: Antiphona Omnes fideles Christiani ad Vulnera Domini recurrite: et invenietis requiem animabus vestris.
blocks.english: Antiphon. All faithful Christians, have recourse to the Wounds of the Lord, and you shall find rest for your souls.

blocks.source: ℣. Sub umbra alarum tuarum protege me, Domine.
blocks.english: ℣. Beneath the shadow of Thy wings protect me, O Lord,

blocks.source: ℟. A facie impiorum, qui me afflixerunt.
blocks.english: ℟. From the face of the wicked who afflicted me.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe Fili Dei vivi, qui afflictos, et ad sacra Vulnera tua confugientes umbra consolationis reficis, et in sinu dulcissimi cordis tui, ad quod per lanceam nobis aditus patefactus est, placide requiescere facis: Largire nobis, ut miseriarum et tentationum aestibus fatigati in sanctissimis Vulneribus tuis quietem ac refrigerium inveniamus, et sub hac umbra sedentes a nullo malorum incursu perturbemur, nec a te separari valeamus. Qui vivis, et regnas, etc.
blocks.english: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who refreshest the afflicted who flee to Thy sacred Wounds with the shade of consolation, and makest them rest gently in the bosom of Thy most sweet Heart, to which access has been opened for us by the spear, grant that, wearied by the heat of miseries and temptations, we may find rest and refreshment in Thy most holy Wounds, and, sitting beneath this shade, be disturbed by no assault of evils, nor be able to be separated from Thee. Who livest and reignest, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Fidelium animae, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful departed, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance, etc.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Haec signa caelis intulit Christus, dum viam finivit. Patri suo proposuit, Paccémque mundo reddidit.
blocks.english:
Christ bore these signs into heaven
When He finished His way;
He set them before His Father
And restored peace to the world.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “Paccémque”; peace is provisional.

blocks.source: Per ista Victor Vulnera, Magna potitur gloria, Honoris sunt insignia, Nobilitatis Symbola.
blocks.english:
Through these Wounds, the Victor
Obtains great glory;
They are marks of honour,
Symbols of nobility.

blocks.source: Laus tibi sit, et Gloria, Rex Christe pro victoria, Per sacra parta Vulnera, Magnae salutis Praetia.
blocks.english:
Praise and glory be to Thee,
Christ the King, for the victory
Won through Thy sacred Wounds,
The price of great salvation.

blocks.source: Antiphona Cum exarserit iracundia ejus, beati omnes, qui sacratissima ejus Vulnera apprehendunt, et in eis confidunt.
blocks.english: Antiphon. When His wrath shall be kindled, blessed are all who take hold of His most sacred Wounds and trust in them.

blocks.source: ℣. Praevenisti eos Domine in benedictionibus.
blocks.english: ℣. Thou hast gone before them, O Lord, with blessings,

blocks.source: ℟. Qui humanae salutis signacula assidue venerantur.
blocks.english: ℟. Who continually venerate the signs of human salvation.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe Fili Dei vivi, qui per proprium sanguinem introivisti in sancta sanctorum, et sedes ad dexteram Dei Patris interpellans pro nobis: Pateant, obsecro, in ejus conspectu Vulnera tua, ut delitescant scelera nostra, et qui factus es Advocatus noster apud Patrem, non obliviscaris servorum in te sperantium, quorum memoriam manibus, pedibus, et lateri tuo tam pretiose insculptam geris. Qui vivis et regnas, etc.
blocks.english: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who through Thine own blood didst enter into the Holy of Holies, and sittest at the right hand of God the Father interceding for us, let Thy Wounds, I beseech Thee, lie open in His sight, that our crimes may be hidden; and Thou who art made our Advocate with the Father, forget not Thy servants who hope in Thee, whose remembrance Thou bearest so preciously engraved upon Thy hands, feet and Side. Who livest and reignest, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Fidelium animae, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful departed, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Converte nos Deus salutaris noster.
blocks.english: ℣. Convert us, O God our Saviour.

blocks.source: ℟. Et averte iram tuam a nobis.
blocks.english: ℟. And turn away Thine anger from us.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance, etc.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, to help, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: O Sacra Jesu Stigmata Firmate nos in gratia, Dum Judicis sententia Partitur justis praemia.
blocks.english:
O sacred marks of Jesus,
Confirm us in grace
When the Judge’s sentence
Distributes rewards to the just.

blocks.source: Vestras tunc alas pandite, In sinum nos recipite, Et nos indignos, gloriae Capaces vestrae reddite.
blocks.english:
Then spread your wings,
Receive us into your bosom,
And render us, though unworthy,
Capable of your glory.

blocks.source: Laus tibi sit, et Gloria, Rex Christe pro victoria, Per sacra parta Vulnera, Magnae salutis Praetia.
blocks.english:
Praise and glory be to Thee,
Christ the King, for the victory
Won through Thy sacred Wounds,
The price of great salvation.

blocks.source: Antiphona Cum apparuerit triumphale crucis signum in caelo, tunc videbunt filium hominis venientem in nubibus caeli.
blocks.english: Antiphon. When the triumphant sign of the Cross appears in heaven, then they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven.

blocks.source: ℣. Signa Vulnerum suorum monstrabit Dominus.
blocks.english: ℣. The Lord shall show the signs of His Wounds,

blocks.source: ℟. Cum judicabit vivos et mortuos, et saeculum per ignem.
blocks.english: ℟. When He shall judge the living and the dead, and the world by fire.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe Fili Dei vivi, qui venturus es in gloria et majestate tua, cum splendore magno quinque Vulnerum tuorum, et judicaturus orbem terrae in aequitate, et populos in justitia: Fac benigne Domine, ut nunc sperent in te, qui noverunt nomen tuum, et coluerunt haec sacrosancta stigmata tua, quorum meritis ad Dextram tuam audire mereantur, venite Benedicti. Qui vivis et regnas, etc.
blocks.english: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who art to come in Thy glory and majesty with the great splendour of Thy five Wounds, and to judge the earth in equity and the peoples in justice, graciously grant, O Lord, that they who have known Thy Name and venerated these most holy marks may now hope in Thee, and through their merits deserve to hear at Thy right hand: Come, ye blessed. Who livest and reignest, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Fidelium animae, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful departed, etc.

blocks.source: O Jesu mei Vulnera, Vos estis mea Gaudia, Vos, mea Desideria, Spes mea, et Fiducia.
blocks.english:
O Wounds of my Jesus,
You are my joys,
You, my desires,
My hope and my confidence.

blocks.source: ℣. Omnis terra adoret te, et psallat tibi.
blocks.english: ℣. Let all the earth adore Thee, and sing to Thee.

blocks.source: ℟. Psalmum dicat sacris Vulneribus tuis, Domine.
blocks.english: ℟. Let it sing a psalm to Thy sacred Wounds, O Lord.

blocks.source: Oratio S. Francisci Xaverii
blocks.english: Prayer of Saint Francis Xavier

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe, Deus cordis mei, per quinque illa Vulnera, quae tibi in cruce noster amor infixit, tuis famulis subveni, quos pretioso sanguine redemisti: Qui vivis et regnas, etc.
blocks.english: O Lord Jesus Christ, God of my heart, through those five Wounds which our love inflicted upon Thee on the Cross, help Thy servants whom Thou hast redeemed with precious blood. Who livest and reignest, etc.

editorialNotes.text: All printed pages of this office were visually compared. Original Latin, existing English, printed hours and abbreviated conclusions are retained. Prepared English hymn stanzas preserve meaningful line divisions. Defective source readings remain explicitly provisional or unresolved. Seven printed hours, without Lauds, and the final prayer attributed to Francis Xavier remain. Each hour’s full and distinct collect is retained. The Matins conclusion continues in the original separate “etc.” row; no omitted doxology or conclusion is expanded from an external edition.
